The claim of stagnation is contradicted by the company’s ability to expand operating margins by 2 percentage points over the last three years [E28] and its fundamental strength in Return on Assets, which sits at 2.02% against a negative sector benchmark of -20.19% [E8]. While the bull cites recent profit growth [E21], this must be weighed against the 3-year compounded profit decline of 4% [E20] and the fact that earnings growth is currently decelerating [E63]. The claim of a turnaround is further undermined by the most recent quarterly data, which shows operating margins have stalled at 2% with zero growth year-over-year [E29]. Furthermore, the bull’s optimism regarding sales is contradicted by the most recent evidence showing a 12% year-over-year decline in sales [E62]. Conceded: [E8], [E19], [E28], [E60]. Investors should also note that the stock’s proximity to its 52-week low [E5] and the total lack of dividend payments [E4] suggest that the market is pricing in these fundamental risks rather than ignoring a hidden opportunity.
